bio12-dna-proteins.title: DNA, replication, genetic code and protein synthesis
bio12-dna-proteins.coverage: Lesson concept checks followed by related subject revision.

questions.prompt: DNA, replication, genetic code and protein synthesis — For template 3′-TAC-5′, what is mRNA?
questions.explanation: Complementary antiparallel RNA pairs A with U and C with G; template TAC gives AUG.

questions.prompt: DNA, replication, genetic code and protein synthesis — What is semiconservative replication?
options: Every base is converted to RNA
Each product has one old and one new strand
Both products contain only old strands
One product is entirely old and the other entirely new
questions.explanation: Original strands each template new complementary strands, conserving one in each daughter double helix.

questions.prompt: DNA, replication, genetic code and protein synthesis — What does code redundancy mean?
options: Several codons can encode one amino acid
Each codon must encode four amino acids
questions.explanation: Synonymous codons can leave the amino-acid sequence unchanged, though other effects can still depend on context.

questions.prompt: DNA, replication, genetic code and protein synthesis — Which molecule brings amino acids to translation machinery?
questions.explanation: Transfer RNA matches anticodon/codon information and delivers the corresponding amino acid to a ribosome.

questions.prompt: DNA, replication, genetic code and protein synthesis — Why may genotype not determine a unique measured phenotype?
options: Gene interactions and environment affect expression/function
questions.explanation: Phenotype emerges through gene expression, product interactions and environmental influences rather than a universal one-genotype one-outcome rule.

questions.prompt: Gene technology, DNA identification and biotechnology — Why use a no-template PCR control?
options: To measure an organism’s abundance directly
To detect contamination or assay artefacts
To prove every sample is positive
questions.explanation: Unexpected target amplification in a negative control undermines confident sample interpretation and requires investigation.

questions.prompt: Natural selection, gene pools, speciation and extinction risk — Does geographic separation immediately establish speciation?
options: Yes, all isolated organisms lose DNA
No, relevant reproductive isolation must develop
Yes, every river makes a new species
questions.explanation: Isolation can permit divergence, but reproductive/species-boundary evidence is needed under the chosen concept.

questions.prompt: Inheritance patterns, Punnett squares and pedigrees — What does an affected aa child imply about two unaffected parents under the stated simple recessive model?
questions.explanation: Each parent supplied a and each remains unaffected, making both heterozygous under complete penetrance and no new mutation.

questions.prompt: Evidence for evolution and reading phylogenies — What does a tree node represent?
options: A guaranteed exact date without scale
questions.explanation: Branching nodes propose common ancestry, and lengths need an explicit scale to represent time or change.

questions.prompt: Natural selection, gene pools, speciation and extinction risk — What distinguishes genetic drift?
options: Individuals changing because they need to
questions.explanation: Sampling effects can change allele frequencies independently of trait advantage, especially in small populations.

questions.prompt: Cell division, meiosis, fertilisation and variation — Between which chromatids does ordinary meiotic crossing over occur?
options: Only sister chromatids of one chromosome
questions.explanation: Corresponding segments exchange between non-sister chromatids in paired homologous chromosomes.

questions.prompt: Gene technology, DNA identification and biotechnology — What does matching band size alone establish?
questions.explanation: Different sequences can share length, and profiles require appropriate loci, controls and probabilistic interpretation.

questions.prompt: Inheritance patterns, Punnett squares and pedigrees — For Aa×Aa under complete dominance, what is recessive phenotype probability?
questions.explanation: The aa outcome occupies one of four equally probable combinations; observed small samples can differ from expectation.

questions.prompt: Gene technology, DNA identification and biotechnology — Where does negatively charged DNA move in the stated gel?
options: No direction under an electric field
questions.explanation: Electrical charge drives migration; smaller fragments usually travel farther under comparable gel conditions.

questions.prompt: Gene technology, DNA identification and biotechnology — What does ligase do in a simplified recombinant method?
questions.explanation: Ligase seals DNA backbone joins; restriction/preparation, delivery and verified expression are separate steps.

questions.prompt: Inheritance patterns, Punnett squares and pedigrees — Does a dominant allele have to be common?
options: Only if it is on an autosome
questions.explanation: Dominance describes expression relationships and does not by itself determine population frequency or fitness.

questions.prompt: Evidence for evolution and reading phylogenies — What most directly indicates homology?
questions.explanation: Homologous structure supports ancestry; similar function can arise independently through convergence.

questions.prompt: Natural selection, gene pools, speciation and extinction risk — Why can antibiotic resistance frequency rise?
options: All susceptible bacteria learn to resist
Resistant variants leave more descendants during exposure
The patient’s cells become resistant bacteria
The drug chooses a useful mutation intentionally
questions.explanation: Heritable variation and differential reproductive success explain population change without teleological mutation.

questions.prompt: Evidence for evolution and reading phylogenies — Which statement about vestigial features is accurate?
options: They prove every ancestor was identical
questions.explanation: Reduction relative to an ancestral condition does not require total uselessness, and context matters.

questions.prompt: Cell division, meiosis, fertilisation and variation — What separates at meiosis I?
questions.explanation: Meiosis I segregates homologues, whereas meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

bio12-homeostasis.unit: Unit 4 – Surviving in a changing environment
bio12-homeostasis.parent: Unit 4 – Surviving in a changing environment
bio12-homeostasis.coverage: Lesson concept checks followed by related subject revision.

questions.prompt: Homeostasis, feedback and thermoregulation — What defines negative feedback?
options: A response opposing the initiating deviation
A response that always amplifies change
questions.explanation: Negative describes the direction of correction relative to the deviation, not whether the outcome is undesirable.

questions.prompt: Homeostasis, feedback and thermoregulation — What primarily distinguishes endothermy?
options: Guaranteed constant temperature at all times
Always living in a hot place
questions.explanation: Heat-source dependence defines the category; both endotherms and ectotherms interact with their environment.

questions.prompt: Homeostasis, feedback and thermoregulation — Which heat-transfer process underlies effective sweating?
questions.explanation: Water evaporation consumes heat from the surface; high humidity can reduce its effectiveness.

questions.prompt: Homeostasis, feedback and thermoregulation — What can vasoconstriction reduce in cool conditions?
options: Peripheral blood flow and heat transfer
questions.explanation: Reduced skin perfusion can limit heat transfer to the environment while other responses also matter.

questions.prompt: Homeostasis, feedback and thermoregulation — Which is a behavioural response?
questions.explanation: Behaviour changes exposure or activity, whereas anatomical structures and physiological responses are distinct categories.

questions.prompt: Animal water, salts, excretion and environmental adaptations — Why is uric acid helpful in dry conditions?
options: It is always more toxic than ammonia
questions.explanation: The water-saving benefit has an energetic cost and does not eliminate every route of water loss.

questions.prompt: Disease transmission, immunity, prevention and population models — What does pandemic primarily concern?
questions.explanation: Geographic extent and severity are different dimensions; endemic also does not mean invariably mild or rare.
